script.base: The book has Dallas laying 7.5 in a 54.5 game, so the morning script is Dallas ahead by about a score in the second half with implied totals DAL 31.0 and ARI 23.5. Javonte Williams, who has 48 carries and 241 rush yards in weeks 5-7, is the clock-killer once Dallas leads. Arizona, as a 7.5-point dog, falls behind and throws: Trey McBride is the primary (32 targets, 230 yards, 209 air yards in that window), with Kendrick Bourne and Michael Wilson at 22 targets each. Pace stays up because 54.5 is a high total, not a slog, so this is a Dallas-control game with Arizona passing volume, not a 17-14 grind.
script.flip1: Dallas is up big by halftime. Williams's carries spike past his 16-per-game weeks 5-7 rate, Dak Prescott and the Dallas receivers (Lamb 35 targets, Pickens 30, Flournoy 17 in that window) lose late snaps, and Arizona abandons the run so the committee of Tyler Allgeier (29 carries, 64 yards) and Zonovan Knight (23 carries, 136 yards) sees the rushing lines die.
script.flip2: Arizona hangs around or it becomes a shootout near the 54.5 total. Both quarterbacks stay in the game, McBride plus Bourne and Wilson and the Dallas trio of Lamb, Pickens and Flournoy all get full snaps, and the run-late edge for Williams never fully arrives.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both legs lost in this Arizona at Dallas game. Knight: Arizona trailed by two scores at half, Allgeier kept the early downs after out-carrying him 29 to 23 over weeks 5-7, and Knight finished at 2 carries for 8 yards, the floor already in the log. The 80-yard game was one long run, and Dallas's 4.92 yards per carry never got a sample. Ferguson: Arizona's middle at 8.34 yards per attempt leaked one crosser, he posted another 19-plus, and Dallas never got the run-late script because a 54.5 total stayed live and Prescott kept throwing to Lamb, Pickens and Flournoy's neighborhood rather than ignoring the tight end. The Ferguson counter is thinner than a 10-target, 32-yard role. The Knight counter is the one that can flip a strong read, which is why this card is flagged rather than sized.
slip_story: Do not parlay the two legs. Knight rush yards over is a standalone lagging-line ticket on the Arizona committee back and it needs this game not to become the blowout flip. Ferguson receiving yards under belongs to the Dallas-control stack, leader runs late with Williams and the receiver room of Lamb, Pickens and Flournoy stays healthy. They share only the moderate Dallas lead branch, something like 31-23. A blowout helps Ferguson under and kills Knight over, so they are opposite on that flip and are not one slip. No touchdown legs and no second market on either player.
